body.text: Which Istanbul station (Söğütlüçeşme, Bostancı, Pendik, Halkalı) should you board from?

Söğütlüçeşme in Kadıköy is the primary Istanbul YHT hub and the best boarding point for almost all visitors staying in central Istanbul. Almost every [Istanbul–Ankara YHT](https://www.tcddtasimacilik.gov.tr/seferler/ankara-istanbul-ankara-yuksek-hizli-tren) and [Istanbul–Konya YHT](https://www.tcddtasimacilik.gov.tr/seferler/yuksek-hizli-tren/) departure originates here, whereas only a small subset of daily trains continues under the Bosphorus to Halkalı on the far western edge of the European side.
Choose your station based on your departure hotel rather than assuming Halkalı is closer to European-side neighborhoods:

body.text: How does Business Class differ from Economy on YHT trains?

Business Class on TCDD Taşımacılık YHT sets (mostly Siemens Velaro or CAF trainsets) uses a spacious 2+1 seating layout with wider reclining seats, extra legroom, individual power outlets, and a quieter passenger mix. Economy Class uses a 2+2 layout that is clean and comfortable for 4.5 hours, but fills completely on peak departures with less elbow room for laptop work.

The price gap between Economy and Business Class is modest by European rail standards, making Business Class strong value if you plan to work, travel with a partner who wants guaranteed pair seating, or simply prefer a calmer cabin. Note that some Economy coaches offer an optional "Economy + meal" fare tier, while full onboard bistro cars serve tea, coffee, sandwiches, and snacks across all classes. You can verify live train positions on the [TCDD Trenim Nerede tracker](https://ebilet.tcddtasimacilik.gov.tr/trenim-nerede).
How early do tickets open and sell out?

TCDD Taşımacılık generally releases YHT high-speed train tickets on the official [TCDD E-Bilet portal](https://ebilet.tcddtasimacilik.gov.tr/) 15 to 30 days ahead of departure (occasionally up to 60 days on selected schedules). Business Class has far fewer seats per trainset and routinely sells out 5 to 10 days before Friday, Sunday, and Monday departures—and within hours of release ahead of religious holidays or school breaks.

Foreign credit cards work on the official TCDD website and mobile app, though some non-Turkish banks trigger 3D-Secure verification prompts. Book directly through ebilet.tcddtasimacilik.gov.tr rather than third-party resellers whenever possible so you pay official fares and can modify or refund tickets easily if plans shift.
How do you reach Söğütlüçeşme smoothly from Sultanahmet or Beyoğlu?

From Sultanahmet, walk or ride the T1 tram to Sirkeci Station and board an eastbound Marmaray suburban train under the Bosphorus—it reaches Söğütlüçeşme in just 12 to 15 minutes with zero road traffic. From Beyoğlu or Taksim, take the funicular to Kabataş (or walk to Karaköy), ride the public ferry to Kadıköy, and take a 10-minute taxi or walk 15 minutes uphill to Söğütlüçeşme.

Alternatively, travelers staying near Şişli, Mecidiyeköy, or Zincirlikuyu can ride the dedicated [İETT Metrobüs rapid bus lane](https://iett.istanbul/icerik/metrobus-hatlari) directly to its eastern terminus right beside Söğütlüçeşme station—just avoid Metrobüs with large suitcases during 08:00–09:30 and 17:30–19:30 commuter peaks.
Use this boarding-day checklist for a calm YHT departure:

items: Arrive 25–30 minutes early: Every passenger and suitcase passes through mandatory X-ray security screening at the station entrance before reaching the platform.
Check coach and seat numbers: Platform displays show exact carriage numbers (Vagon) so you can wait near the right door before the train pulls in.
Use Marmaray for luggage: Sirkeci and Yenikapı Marmaray stations have elevators and wide escalators, avoiding Bosphorus bridge traffic jams completely.
Keep passport handy: Ticket inspectors check the digital QR code on your phone alongside your passport or Turkish ID number entered during booking.

faq.q: How long is the YHT train from Istanbul to Ankara and Konya?
faq.a: From Söğütlüçeşme, the YHT takes roughly 4 hours 15 minutes to 4 hours 35 minutes to reach Ankara Gar, and 4 hours 50 minutes to 5 hours 15 minutes to reach Konya (with a brief stop at Eskişehir).

faq.q: Is it better to take the YHT train or fly from Istanbul to Ankara?
faq.a: City-center to city-center, the YHT train often matches or beats flying once you factor in 60-minute airport transfers to Istanbul Airport (IST) and Ankara Esenboğa (ESB), early security check-in, and baggage claim.

faq.q: Does the YHT go all the way to Cappadocia?
faq.a: No. There is no direct high-speed rail station in Cappadocia. Travelers either take the YHT to Konya (followed by a 3-hour private road transfer to Göreme/Ürgüp) or fly directly from Istanbul to Kayseri (ASR) or Nevşehir (NAV).

faq.q: Can I bring large suitcases on TCDD YHT trains?
faq.a: Yes. Each coach has overhead racks for cabin bags and dedicated luggage bays near the carriage doors for full-sized suitcases, with no strict airline-style weight fees for normal personal luggage.

faq.q: Is there Wi-Fi on YHT high-speed trains?
faq.a: Selected Siemens Velaro sets offer onboard Wi-Fi, though speeds drop through tunnels between İzmit and Bilecik. Downloading offline files or using a local Turkish mobile data plan is more reliable for uninterrupted work.

faq.q: Where does the YHT arrive in Ankara and Konya?
faq.a: In Ankara, YHT trains terminate at the modern Ankara YHT Gar right in the city center (connected to the Ankaray metro at Maltepe). In Konya, trains stop at Selçuklu YHT and terminate at central Konya Gar, 10 minutes by taxi from the Mevlana Museum.
